Consult Summary:
- Adult patient with 2-day history of constant, gradually worsening lower abdominal pain (below umbilicus), with nausea and feeling hot/sweaty.
- Clinician suspects urinary tract infection (UTI) vs gastrointestinal or pregnancy-related cause; empirical antibiotics started, pregnancy test advised, and safety-netting provided.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute lower abdominal pain: Onset ~2 days ago, gradual and worsening; localized below the umbilicus; burning quality; tender/sore to palpation; constant but patient able to function.
- Associated symptoms: Felt hot/sweaty; mild nausea; no vomiting; no diarrhea; bowels normal currently (constipation last week resolved).
- Review of systems: No dysuria or stinging; urine noted “pink” in color; increased urinary frequency (patient has also been drinking more fluids); no shortness of breath, cough, palpitations, headaches, or vision problems.
- Exam: No vitals or physical exam documented.
- Differential diagnosis: UTI; gastrointestinal cause; pregnancy-related cause.

Issue 2:
- Urinary symptoms/possible hematuria: Reports “pink” urine; uncertain if blood present; increased frequency; denies dysuria.
- Plan related to this issue described below (empiric UTI treatment, hydration, consider further testing if no improvement).

Issue 3:
- Contraception and pregnancy consideration: On etonogestrel implant (Implanon) inserted ~1 year ago; sexually active with same partner; last intercourse ~4 days ago; last STI screen normal ~6 months ago; still having periods; last period reported as “about three weeks ago… two weeks ago” (conflict noted).
- Pregnancy considered unlikely but possible; advised to perform a pregnancy test.

Medications:
- Trimethoprim — 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days; route and tablet strength not documented (new prescription e-sent to pharmacy).
- Acetaminophen (paracetamol) — dose/route/frequency not documented (advised for pain).
- Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) — in situ; inserted ~1 year ago.

Allergies:
- Not documented.

Past Medical History:
- Generally well.
- No prior surgeries.
- No prior similar symptoms.
- Family history: No relevant bowel or related conditions reported.

Social History:
- Lives in a shared house with two roommates.
- Occupation: Accountant.
- Non-smoker.
- Alcohol: Social use; not above typical levels.

Preventative History:
- STI screen normal ~6 months ago.
- Other preventive care (cervical screening, mammogram, prostate testing, fecal occult blood test, bone density, vaccinations, optometry, skin check): Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Examination findings: Not documented.

Plan:
- Start empiric UTI treatment: Trimethoprim 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days.
- Perform a home pregnancy test today to exclude pregnancy.
- Symptomatic care: Hydration; acetaminophen as needed for pain; may try cranberry juice.
- Safety-net advice: Seek review urgently if worsening abdominal pain, persistent/high fevers or feeling very hot/sweaty, or vomiting.
- Follow-up: Reassess in a few days if no improvement or sooner if symptoms worsen.
- If symptoms persist or worsen: Consider urine dipstick/urinalysis and culture, and further evaluation for gastrointestinal or gynecologic causes as indicated.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Allergies not documented; no vitals or physical exam; no urinalysis or culture performed; pregnancy test not yet performed; medication tablet strength and route for trimethoprim not documented; acetaminophen dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Internal conflicts: Patient name addressed as “Tim” and later “Kim” (conflict noted). Last menstrual period reported as “three weeks ago” then corrected to “two weeks ago” (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Minor disfluencies; otherwise understandable.
